ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Layer Gradient Cosine Between Text and Image Losses
PROPOSAL: Take a publicly released autoregressive model that reads and writes both text and discrete image tokens, and measure how text-loss gradients and image-loss gradients agree in each transformer layer. Draw 2000 caption-image pairs, split them into separate data slices, compute both gradients for every layer on each slice, and record cosine similarity plus the fraction of parameters whose gradient signs differ. Plot both quantities against depth with intervals across slices.
CONTROLS: Compare the cross-modal cosine with the cosine between two text slices and between two image slices at each layer. Repeat on a second checkpoint of the same model, and on three random orders of the slices.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Cross-modal cosine should sit below the within-modality values in the middle layers. The finding is undermined if both within-modality values are as low as the cross-modal one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Where Conflict Emerges During Training From Scratch
PROPOSAL: Train a one-billion-parameter autoregressive transformer from scratch on a mixture of captions and discrete image tokens, and log the per-layer gradient cosine between the text loss and the image loss every 1000 steps. Track how the depth profile moves over training, and compare it with the loss curves of each modality. Save checkpoints at fixed intervals so that a later analysis can probe them.
CONTROLS: Run the same logging on a text-only model and on an image-only model of the same size to get within-modality references. Repeat training over three seeds. Use identical data order across the mixture and single-modality runs.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: Conflict should appear early in the middle layers and fade as training progresses. The idea fails if the profile is flat across layers at every checkpoint.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token Statistics of Images Versus Text
PROPOSAL: Measure token entropy, local repetition, compressibility and long-range dependence for text from a web corpus and for image tokens from three vector quantisation tokenizers applied to the same pictures. Then train a small 150-million-parameter transformer on each pairing and record the per-layer gradient cosine between modalities. Correlate the gap in each statistic with the strength and depth of conflict.
CONTROLS: Compare each statistic gap against the gap between two text corpora. Include a pairing of two image tokenizers as a within-modality reference. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Larger gaps in entropy and repetition should go with stronger conflict. The correlation analysis fails to support the idea if every statistic correlates near zero.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Separate Normalisation Per Modality in a Shared Transformer
PROPOSAL: Give each modality its own normalisation scale and shift in every layer of a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive transformer, while attention and feed-forward weights stay shared. Train on captions and discrete image tokens and measure steps to a target score on text-to-image generation and visual question answering. Add the gradient cosine profile before and after the change.
CONTROLS: Compare with a fully shared model of the same size trained on identical data. Compare with a variant that adds a normalisation scale per layer but shares it between modalities. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: The change should reduce middle-layer conflict and shorten steps to target. The idea fails if the shared-scale variant behaves the same as the modality-specific one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Low-Rank Modality Adapters in Middle Layers
PROPOSAL: Insert low-rank adapters, one set per modality, into the middle third of the layers of a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive transformer, with the rest of the weights shared. Train on captions and discrete image tokens, route each token to its adapter by modality, and evaluate image generation and visual question answering. Measure the cross-modal gradient cosine in the adapted layers.
CONTROLS: Compare with the fully shared model, with adapters placed in the first third of the layers, and with adapters of doubled rank at the same total parameter count. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Middle-layer adapters should lower cross-modal conflict more than early-layer adapters. The idea fails if the doubled-rank variant gives the same scores as the middle-layer variant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Projection as a Causal Test of Conflict
PROPOSAL: Train two autoregressive transformers on the same mixture of captions and image tokens. In one, project away from the image gradient the component that opposes the text gradient at each layer, and do the same in the other direction on alternate steps. Record steps to target scores and the layers where the projection removes the most gradient. Relate those layers to the measured conflict profile.
CONTROLS: Compare with an unprojected model on identical data order, and with a projection applied to randomly chosen layers. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Projection should remove the most gradient in the middle layers and speed up early training. The idea fails if random-layer projection gives the same speed-up.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Codebook Size and Modality Conflict
PROPOSAL: Train 600-million-parameter autoregressive transformers on captions combined with image tokens from tokenizers whose codebooks hold 1024, 4096 and 16384 entries. Record the per-layer gradient cosine between modalities and the depth where conflict peaks for each codebook. Relate the peak depth and strength to token entropy and to the repetition rate of the image-token streams.
CONTROLS: Compare against a text-only model for a within-modality reference, and hold the data order and the training steps fixed across codebooks. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Smaller codebooks should produce more repetitive streams and stronger conflict at shallower depth. The idea fails if peak depth is identical for all three codebooks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Selective Sharing Across Depth
PROPOSAL: Split the layers of a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive transformer into early, middle and late thirds and give each modality its own weights in one third at a time while sharing the other two. Train every variant on captions and discrete image tokens for the same number of steps. Evaluate generation and visual question answering, and measure the cross-modal gradient cosine in each third.
CONTROLS: Compare with a fully shared model and with a fully separate pair of models at the same total parameter count. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 3500
PREDICTION: Separating the middle third should recover most of the gain of full separation. The idea fails if separating the early third works as well.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality Conflict Across Model Scales
PROPOSAL: Train autoregressive transformers of 150 million, 600 million and 1.5 billion parameters on the same mixture of captions and image tokens, keeping the data order and the token budget per run constant. Measure the per-layer gradient cosine between modalities through training and record how the depth and strength of conflict change with scale. Fit a simple trend of peak conflict against parameter count.
CONTROLS: Compare against single-modality runs of each size to separate scale effects from modality effects. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: Conflict should grow with scale in the middle layers. The trend fails to hold if the largest model shows weaker conflict than the smallest.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image Editing and Generation With a Modality-Aware Model
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive model with modality-specific normalisation and adapters in the middle layers, then fine-tune it on instruction-based image editing and text-to-image generation. Evaluate on GenEval, an editing benchmark with human preference ratings, and visual question answering. Report scores with intervals over seeds and note which tasks gain the most.
CONTROLS: Compare against the fully shared model with identical fine-tuning, and against the same model with adapters removed at test time. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Editing should gain more than plain generation because it needs both understanding and synthesis. The idea fails if the fully shared model reaches the same editing scores.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-Wise Cosine Between Text and Image Gradients
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B autoregressive transformer on interleaved captions and discrete image tokens from a public image-text corpus. At regular checkpoints along training, compute the gradient of the text loss and of the image-token loss on separate data slices, flatten the attention and feed-forward parameters of each layer, and record cosine similarity per layer. Summarise the result as a depth profile with intervals over slices.
CONTROLS: Compare the text-versus-image cosine against the cosine between two text slices at the same layer. Compare against the cosine between text gradients and gradients from text with permuted token order. Compare against the cosine at an earlier stage of training. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Cosine should fall below the text-only level in middle layers. The claim fails if text-versus-image cosine matches the text-only level at every layer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Direction Agreement Across Layers of a Mixed-Modality Transformer
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 1.5B decoder-only transformer on a mixture of captions and quantised image tokens drawn from a public image-text corpus. Every 500 updates, back-propagate the text loss and the image-token loss on separate data slices, concatenate the parameters of each layer, and store the cosine between the two gradients. Present the outcome as a depth curve with intervals over slices.
CONTROLS: Compare the text-versus-image cosine against the cosine between a gradient and the optimiser momentum at the same layer. Compare against the cosine between parameters across two initialisations. Compare against the cosine at a later stage of training. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Cosine should fall below the momentum-aligned level in middle layers. The claim fails if text-versus-image cosine matches the momentum-aligned level at every layer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token Statistics and the Depth Profile of Modality Conflict
PROPOSAL: Train 600M-parameter autoregressive transformers on streams built from natural text and from image tokens with 1024-entry and 8192-entry codebooks, and measure the per-layer gradient cosine between modalities in each run. Compute token entropy and repetition rate of each stream. Relate the depth at which conflict peaks to those statistics across runs.
CONTROLS: Vary the codebook entry count while holding model depth fixed. Vary the image token order between raster and column order while holding the codebook fixed. Compare the conflict profile against that from two text corpora with different entropy. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 880
PREDICTION: Conflict should peak at a shallower depth when image tokens are more repetitive. The claim fails if the peak depth stays unchanged across all codebooks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimisation Choices and the Depth Profile of Modality Conflict
PROPOSAL: Train 600M-parameter autoregressive transformers on one mixture of natural text and image tokens with an 8192-entry codebook under several optimiser choices, and measure the per-layer gradient cosine between modalities in each run. Compute the update norm and loss spike rate of each run. Relate the depth at which conflict peaks to those quantities across runs.
CONTROLS: Vary the warmup length while holding model depth fixed. Vary the weight decay between low and high values while holding the peak step size fixed. Compare the conflict profile against that from two optimisers with different update rules. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 880
PREDICTION: Conflict should peak at a shallower depth when updates are larger. The claim fails if the peak depth stays unchanged across all optimisers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-Specific Adapters in a Shared Autoregressive Transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B autoregressive model on a mixture of captions and image tokens, giving each modality its own normalisation scales and low-rank adapters in the middle layers while attention stays shared. Evaluate text-to-image generation on GenEval and COCO captions, and visual question answering on VQAv2 and GQA. Report the scores together with the number of training steps to reach a target loss.
CONTROLS: Compare against a fully shared model of the same parameter count trained on the same mixture. Compare against a model with adapters in all layers. Compare mixed-modality training against single-modality training. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Gains should appear on the generation benchmarks first. The claim fails if the fully shared model reaches the same scores in the same number of steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-Specific Adapters Evaluated on Text-Only Language Tasks
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 1.5B autoregressive model on documents from a text corpus only, equipping the middle layers with their own normalisation scales and low-rank adapters per document type while attention is shared. Score next-token loss on withheld documents and accuracy on HellaSwag and ARC. Give the scores plus the training steps needed to reach a target loss.
CONTROLS: Compare against a fully shared model of the same parameter count trained on the same corpus. Compare against a model with adapters in all layers. Compare document-type training against single-document-type training. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Gains should appear on the long-document tasks first. The claim fails if the fully shared model reaches the same scores in the same number of steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Convergence Speed of Modality-Aware Autoregressive Models
PROPOSAL: Run a modality-aware 1.5B autoregressive model beside a fully shared one of the same size on identical captions and image tokens, with evaluation every 2000 steps. Note the steps needed to reach target GenEval and VQAv2 scores, then the final scores. Fit time-to-target curves with intervals over seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare steps to target against the fully shared model of the same size on the same data. Compare against a model with a separate image output head. Compare final scores on the generation and understanding benchmarks. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 1300
PREDICTION: The modality-aware model should reach target scores in fewer steps. The claim fails if time-to-target curves overlap within intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Smoothness of Modality-Aware Autoregressive Models
PROPOSAL: Train a modality-aware 1.5B autoregressive model and a fully shared one of the same size on identical captions and image tokens, evaluating every 2000 steps. Log the gradient norm and how many loss spikes occur, together with the final training loss. Fit smoothness curves with intervals over seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare gradient norm against the fully shared model of the same size on the same data. Compare against a model with a larger step size. Compare final training loss on text tokens and image tokens. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 1300
PREDICTION: The modality-aware model should show fewer spikes. The claim fails if smoothness curves overlap within intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Simplicity Check Against Branching Designs
PROPOSAL: Pretrain our modality-aware autoregressive model at 3B parameters on 200B tokens of captions and image tokens, then evaluate it on GenEval, DPG-Bench, VQAv2 and MMBench. Report each score with intervals over seeds, and the parameter count of every design that takes part in the comparison.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed model against a fully shared model of the same parameter count. Compare against a branch-per-modality design with the same parameter count. Compare against a model with an added semantic encoder. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The proposed model should come close to the branching design on generation scores with fewer parameters. The claim fails if the fully shared model lands within intervals of the proposed model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checkpoint and Tokenizer Variants of the Modality-Aware Model
PROPOSAL: Pretrain our modality-aware autoregressive model at 3B parameters on 200B tokens of captions and image tokens, then evaluate several of its own variants on GenEval, DPG-Bench, VQAv2 and MMBench. Report each score with intervals over seeds, and the training token count of every variant that takes part in the comparison.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed model against its own checkpoint at half the training tokens. Compare against a variant with a larger tokenizer vocabulary. Compare against the same model with a longer context length. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The proposed model should gain on generation scores as training progresses. The claim fails if the half-training checkpoint lands within intervals of the final model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Layer Gradient Conflict Between Text and Image Losses
PROPOSAL: Take a trained 1.5B autoregressive model and, on a set of held-out slices, calculate the text-loss gradient and the image-loss gradient for each layer, then store the cosine and the fraction of coordinates where the signs disagree. Rank layers by conflict and track the ranking over checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Compare against the conflict between two text slices at each layer. Compare against the conflict between two image slices. Compare against the conflict after projecting out the shared direction. Repeat over 3 seeds of slice sampling.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Middle layers should show the lowest cosine. The idea fails if the ranking changes completely between checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Modality Training Loss Gap in Autoregressive Models
PROPOSAL: Take a trained 1.5B autoregressive model and, on a set of held-out slices, calculate the text loss and the image-token loss at each checkpoint, then store the gap between the two and the rate at which each declines. Rank checkpoints by gap and track the ranking over training.
CONTROLS: Compare against the gap between two text slices at each checkpoint. Compare against the gap between two image slices. Compare against the gap after rescaling both quantities to the same range. Repeat over 3 seeds of slice sampling.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Early checkpoints should show the largest gap. The idea fails if the ranking changes completely between checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Controlled Token Streams for Conflict Attribution
PROPOSAL: Build synthetic token streams that vary one statistic at a time, such as entropy, local repetition and long-range dependence, and train 150M transformers on mixtures of two streams. Measure the gradient cosine between the streams per layer. Fit a regression from stream statistics to the depth and strength of conflict.
CONTROLS: Compare each mixture against two samples of the same stream. Compare against a mixture whose streams share the same entropy. Compare against real text and image-token streams. Repeat over 3 seeds of stream generation.
COST: 410
PREDICTION: Entropy mismatch should drive conflict in early layers and dependence mismatch in later layers. The idea fails if the regression explains little variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-Wise Probes of Abstraction in Autoregressive Image-Text Models
PROPOSAL: Freeze a trained 1.5B autoregressive model and fit linear probes on the output of each layer for object category, caption topic and token identity. Measure probe accuracy per layer on image-token and text sequences. Fit a regression from layer depth to probe accuracy and to abstraction level.
CONTROLS: Compare each probe against probes fit on two samples of the same stream. Compare against probes whose targets have the same entropy. Compare against probes on untrained weights. Repeat over 3 seeds of probe initialization.
COST: 410
PREDICTION: Abstraction should rise towards the middle layers and fall near the output. The idea fails if the regression explains little variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-Specific Normalisation With Fully Shared Attention
PROPOSAL: Give each modality separate scale and shift parameters in every normalisation layer of a 1.5B autoregressive transformer while sharing all attention and feed-forward weights. Train on captions and image tokens and measure the time to target GenEval and VQAv2 scores, and the final scores.
CONTROLS: Compare against a fully shared model with the same parameter count. Compare against a branch-per-modality design. Compare against a variant with normalisation parameters shared across modalities. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 1900
PREDICTION: The shared-attention design should capture most of the gain of branching. The idea fails if it scores the same as the fully shared model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion Decoder Head on an Autoregressive Backbone
PROPOSAL: Attach a diffusion decoder to a 1.5B autoregressive transformer that predicts image latents from the backbone states, and train on captions and image data. Measure the time to target GenEval and VQAv2 scores, and the final scores.
CONTROLS: Compare against a fully shared model with the same parameter count. Compare against a branch-per-modality design. Compare against a variant with the decoder detached from the backbone. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 1900
PREDICTION: The decoder head should capture most of the gain of branching. The idea fails if it scores the same as the fully shared model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Surgery as a Diagnostic for Modality Conflict
PROPOSAL: Train 1.5B autoregressive models with and without conflict-aware gradient projection, which removes the component of one modality's gradient that opposes the other's, applied per layer. Measure steps to target and final scores on GenEval and VQAv2, and relate gains to the measured conflict per layer.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unprojected model with the same data order. Compare projection in all layers against projection in the layers with the most conflict. Compare against a projection that uses the gradient of a different loss. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: Projection should speed up training mainly in the layers with the strongest conflict. The idea fails if projecting all layers gives the same gains as projecting the layers with the most conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a Vision-Language Teacher Into an Autoregressive Model
PROPOSAL: Distil a pretrained vision-language model into a 1.5B autoregressive model by matching its output distribution on captions and image tokens, applied per layer. Measure steps to target and final scores on GenEval and VQAv2, and relate gains to the teacher size.
CONTROLS: Compare against the student trained without teacher outputs with the same data order. Compare distillation from all layers against distillation from the last layers. Compare against distillation from a teacher of a different size. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: Distillation should speed up training mainly in the early steps. The idea fails if distilling from all layers gives the same gains as distilling from the last layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy and Repetition of Image Tokens Versus Text Tokens
PROPOSAL: Compute token entropy, n-gram repetition and compressibility on 100000 text sequences and 100000 image-token sequences from public corpora, with image tokens from three tokenizers. Measure per-layer gradient cosine for a 300M model trained on each pairing, and correlate conflict strength with the statistic gaps.
CONTROLS: Compare each statistic gap against the gap between two text corpora. Compare against the gap between two image corpora. Compare against the gap between two tokenizers on the same images. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: Larger statistic gaps should align with stronger conflict. The idea fails if the correlation is near zero for all statistics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reconstruction Quality of Image Tokenizers Across Codebooks
PROPOSAL: Compute reconstruction error, perceptual distance and codebook usage on 100000 images from public corpora, with tokenizers of three codebook types. Measure the reconstruction fidelity for a 300M model trained on each tokenizer, and correlate reconstruction quality with the codebook usage.
CONTROLS: Compare each tokenizer score against the score between two image corpora. Compare against the score between two codebook sizes. Compare against the score between two tokenizers on the same images. Repeat over 3 seeds of data order.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: Larger codebooks should align with better reconstruction. The idea fails if the correlation is near zero for all tokenizers.
